messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: INC-5022 fired for 'hosted-inference-high-err-rate' -> threshold: 5xx rate > 3% (service: hosted-inference). Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-5022 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy 'inference-service-oncall' triggered. Primary: alice (no ack after 2 mins), Secondary: ben (paged), Manager: carla (queued). Escalation details:
```
escalation_level: 2
targets: [alice, ben, carla]
ack_status: [alice: no, ben: no, carla: pending]
reason: primary missed ack (mobile DND?) -> auto-escalate
```
alice: i'm getting the page but my phone is on DND, trying from laptop — slack notification kinda delayed for me. taking it now.
ben: i'm in a meeting, can ack and triage in ~5 unless someone else can take.
carla: i'm available if it escalates further. do we know customer impact yet?
david: looking at metrics, 5xx spike from model-serving instances in us-west-2, error pattern looks like KV cache eviction spike after a rollout. throwing extra logs to cloudwatch now.
eve: i'm on the bridge in case we need to rollback. joining call 2.
alice: acked. quick snapshot of errors: "kv_cache_miss -> failed to allocate kv buffer" on gpu-12-*, repeated after model rollout at 21:15 UTC.
frank: can we route traffic off the new variant? we have canary traffic still in prod only 8%, but errors show amplified.
ben: if alice has it, i'll stand by. alice, can you confirm whether the new variant is pinned to quantized kernels? that could trigger allocation pattern change.
alice: yep, variant-v3 was rolled with new kernel selection. the rollout job shows 30% in progress 21:14 -> 21:16. looks like some nodes hit memory pressure.
david: temporary mitigation: reduce concurrency and shift canary back to variant-v2. executing router change now. command: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/shift -d '{"from":"variant-v3","to":"variant-v2","percent":8}'`
incident-bot: Router change accepted, shifting 8% of traffic off variant-v3 -> variant-v2.
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: secondary (ben) was paged because primary didn't ack within timeout window. No manager escalation executed.
ben: just saw the router change, thanks. i'll verify backends. logs show some nodes recovering.
eve: i'm increasing GPU pool autoscale by +2 instances in us-west-2 as a quick buffer: `infra scale gpus --region us-west-2 --count +2`
carla: customer impact? any 5xx seen by customers? severity?
david: our frontend error rate peaked to 2.8% of user requests for 6 minutes — sessions affected: ~420 unique tokens. Not wide outage but customer-visible errors for some requests hitting the canary.
alice: mitigating: canary traffic fully shifted back, a handful of pods still recycling. will watch for 10 minutes.
frank: going to pin an alert to ensure no re-rolls happen for the model until postmortem. please add a release hold in the console.
carla: thanks team. please post short incident summary in #incidents after stable and open a postmortem ticket. assign to alice + david.
alice: will do. putting incident severity: P2; root cause initial: kernel selection + insufficient allocation fallback, allowed canary to expose bug.
ben: acking follow-up: i'll check PD policy to see why manager didn't get paged — there was a brief race where the Slack integration delayed ack visibility and PD auto-escalated but then retracted. Might be an integration race.
incident-bot: Incident resolved for INC-5022: error rate returned to baseline at 21:34 UTC after traffic shift and autoscale.
carla: nice work. we should add a safeguard: block model kernel changes during rolling deploys for 24h after major changes. noted for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
